judged_text: The BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS entries are lowercased (line 71) but the guest emails compared against them at line 77 are not normalized, so `blacklistedGuestEmails.includes(guest)` fails to match case-variant addresses. An operator who sets BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS=blocked@example.com to stop a specific address from being contacted (compliance/opt-out blocklist) is trivially bypassed by submitting "Blocked@Example.com" — the address passes the filter, is written as a BookingAttendee, and is emailed the full booking details (description, location, video call URL and password), defeating the control the env var exists to provide; the same missing normalization also lets a caller re-add an existing attendee under a case variant.

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, `blacklistedGuestEmails` is normalized to lowercase (`.map((email) => email.toLowerCase())`), but the comparison uses `!blacklistedGuestEmails.includes(guest)` where `guest` is not lowercased. Since emails are case-variant strings, a user can bypass `BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS=blocked@example.com` by submitting `Blocked@Example.com`, which will not match the lowercase blocklist and will be persisted/emailed. The same lack of normalization exists in the duplicate check `guest === attendee.email`, allowing re-adding an existing attendee via case variants.
